item.title: Premier League confirms streaming service – and it’s not called Premflix
item.description: The Premier League is to launch a streaming platform in Singapore that could pave the way for a global direct-to-consumer “Premflix” product, CEO Richard Masters has confirmed. item.title: Birmingham driving service sector boom
item.description: Birmingham has been at the front of a “service sector boom”, according to new research from Oxford Economics, helping to drive job creation across the wider region. item.description: The number of Neets, or young people not in education, employment or training, has increased to nearly 1m, official data has indicated, heightening fears over the long-term health of the UK economy. item.title: Consumer confidence slips in latest setback for Labour
item.description: Consumer confidence slipped slightly in February despite hopes of a turnaround, adding to fears the UK economy could slump this year. A closely-monitored survey conducted by the research firm GfK said consumer confidence dropped by three points to -19. item.title: Universal handed £6m of taxpayer cash to film Hamnet despite raking in profits of £810m
item.description: American filmmaking giant Universal was handed a £5.7 million government subsidy to make period drama Hamnet even though the studio generated £810 million in profit last year.
